text:
anika: quick heads-up — after the RBAC prune that merged last night, cert-rotator started failing unwraps in eu-west1 and apac-south1. model-router mTLS handshakes from edge-proxy are dropping.

leo: is this only edge-proxy->model-router or broader?

anika: observed on edge-proxy -> model-router path. cert-rotator logs show KMS denies when trying to unwrap KEK.

security-bot: Alert: 9 failed mTLS handshakes (eu-west1, apac-south1). KMS error: "PermissionDenied: cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt denied for principal serviceAccount:rotator@infra.redwood.com"

maya: snippet from cert-rotator:
```
2026-03-19T03:12:45Z cert-rotator ERROR unwrap_key: KMS PermissionDenied: serviceAccount:rotator@infra.redwood.com for key projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/cert-unwrap
```

josh: I reviewed PR #4891 (RBAC prune) — it removed some legacy alias mappings. looks like the explicit binding for cert-rotator on the specific key got dropped.

ops-oncall: severity: users seeing 5xx for inference. Need quick mitigation to restore unwraps.

leo: short-term plan: add back a minimal, scoped IAM binding for the cert-unwrap key to the rotator SA. keep it narrowly scoped to the single key & project.

anika: proposed gcloud command (scoped):
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding cert-unwrap \
  --location global --keyring keystore \
  --member serviceAccount:rotator@infra.redwood.com \
  --role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```

maya: +1. while we apply, add a Condition restricting by source VPC or tag for eu/apac if possible.

josh: for compliance we need an audit export of KMS.Decrypt/UseToDecrypt attempts from 02:45-03:30Z. push to incident bucket and attach to ticket.

security-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-342 severity=P2 (multi-region). Assigned: eng-security, infra-oncall.

ops-oncall: applied scoped binding and restarted cert-rotator. unwraps resumed; mTLS handshakes started recovering. Monitoring 30m.

anika: immediate mitigation worked. root-cause: RBAC prune removed reconciliation mapping that surfaced the role-alias -> explicit key IAM binding for scheduled rotator SA.

leo: long-term fixes:
- reintroduce reconciliation rule with exceptions for scheduled jobs (cert-rotator, rotation-poller)
- update cert-rotator to use a short-lived unwrap token or cached symmetric key served from control plane to reduce KMS dependency
- add pre-merge RBAC check that flags removal of principals used by active cronjobs/schedulers

maya: postmortem checklist:
- timeline and exact IAM delta from PR #4891
- audit export verification (who attempted decrypt)
- ensure no plaintext material leaked to logs or storage
- update runbook with emergency scoped-binding steps

josh: ran audit query — only rotator@infra attempted Decrypt during the window. exported ndjson to gs://redwood-security-incidents/INC-2026-342/2026-03-19-kms-decrypt-export.ndjson

anika: follow-ups (INC-2026-342):
- add RBAC reconciliation exception + unit tests (anika)
- implement control-plane short-lived unwrap token + cache (leo)
- extend audit export retention for KMS Decrypt events to 1y and update compliance docs (josh)
- add pre-merge check for scheduled-service principals and update runbook (maya)

ops-oncall: leaving PR #4891 rollback as a last-resort option; scoped binding is lower risk and documented.

security-bot: Reminder: attach PR diff, IAM policy change, and oncall approval to incident ticket for compliance review.

compliance: acknowledged; we'll review the export and confirm retention requirements. tagging legal for any contract implications.

anika: I'll add the PR link, IAM diff, and who authorized the emergency binding to the incident. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

leo: suggestion — add a lightweight check in the RBAC prune job: diff the candidate policy against a list of principals that appear in active scheduled jobs; block or warn if there's overlap.

maya: +1 filing ENG-SRE ticket. also adding an acceptance test to CI that simulates KMS deny for key unwrap to catch regressions.

josh: making a compliance follow-up to confirm 1y retention is fine given customer contracts.

anika: closing triage thread; ping @ops-oncall if anything recurs.
